compliance.summary: The robot operated at the boundary of its ODD, with multiple axes showing less than a 15% margin to their limits, specifically max acceleration (0.10-0.15 m/s² vs <=10 m/s²), max speed (0.0 m/s vs <=2.0 m/s), obstacle density (0.01-0.03 vs <=0.7), and clearance index (0.80-0.95 vs >=0.3). Additionally, lighting conditions degraded to 'dim' in one window, severely impacting camera perception, even though 'dim' is technically within ODD limits.

report.executive_summary: The robot operated within an indoor residential environment, but its performance was flagged as BOUNDARY due to operating close to several ODD limits. Critical concerns arose from severely degraded camera perception in dim lighting conditions during one window, which posed a high operational risk despite being technically within ODD lighting parameters. Operators should investigate the lighting situation and robot's proximity control.

key_findings.perception: Lighting conditions varied from moderate to dim, degrading camera performance, with obstacle density remaining low between 2.1% and 3.2% across hardwood terrain.
key_findings.motion: The robot primarily exhibited rotational motion, with maximum acceleration at 0.15 m/s², maximum roll at 4.99 degrees, and maximum pitch at 6.95 degrees, all well within ODD.
key_findings.safety: The robot maintained a safe minimum proximity of 2.1 meters to obstacles, with a clearance index ranging from 0.80 to 0.95, which triggered a warning due to a low margin (7.14%) to its ODD limit of >=0.3.
key_findings.temporal_trends: The perception environment showed a degrading trend primarily due to darkening lighting conditions, while motion stability showed an improving trend.

lighting_conditions.description: Ambient light level for camera perception. bright=well-lit, clear visibility; moderate=typical indoor; dim=reduced but functional; dark=camera cannot function (OUT OF ODD)

terrain_type.description: Ground surface type. Assess from camera view of floor. List specific materials visible. Not designed for high-pile carpet, shag rugs, or any outdoor terrain.

obstacle_density.description: Fraction of BEV area occupied by obstacles (0-1). Computed from BEV occupancy map, not camera. 0.0=empty, 0.7=high density, >0.7=extreme clutter (OUT OF ODD).

clearance_index.description: Navigability index computed from BEV map (0-1). 1.0=clear path, 0.3=narrow but passable. <0.3=path blocked (OUT OF ODD). Measures path navigability, not tidiness.

stairs_present.description: Binary check for accessible stairs. 1=stairs are present and accessible to the robot (OUT OF ODD). 0=no stairs or stairs are blocked off (IN ODD). Assess from BEV map by looking for sharp, sustained elevation changes.

human_present.description: Binary human detection. 1=human visible anywhere in camera frame (OUT OF ODD - halt required). 0=no humans detected (IN ODD). Assess from CAMERA only, not BEV. Any person visible = violation.

animal_present.description: Binary animal detection. 1=animal visible anywhere in camera frame (OUT OF ODD - halt required). 0=no animals detected (IN ODD). Assess from CAMERA only, not BEV. Any animal visible = violation.

max_speed_mps.description: Maximum linear velocity of the robot's center of mass. Normal indoor navigation speed. Exceeding this limit is considered high-speed operation and is OUT OF ODD.

max_accel_mps2.description: Maximum linear acceleration of the robot's center of mass. Brief, reactive accelerations up to 10 m/s² are expected during obstacle avoidance. Sustained high acceleration is not.

max_roll_deg.description: Maximum absolute roll angle of the robot chassis. This represents the limit for stable operation on flat or gently sloped indoor surfaces. Exceeding 15 degrees indicates an unstable situation, potentially due to an obstacle or terrain anomaly.

max_pitch_deg.description: Maximum absolute pitch angle of the robot chassis. Corresponds to navigating ramps up to 15 degrees. Exceeding this indicates a slope that is too steep and OUT OF ODD.
